chunks: From him, from Aḥmad ibn Muḥammad, from Ibn Maḥbūb, from al-Faḍl ibn Yūnus, who said:
I asked Abā al-Ḥasan al-Awwal عليه السلام. I said: If a woman sees purity before sunset, what should she do regarding the salat (prayer)?

He said: “If she sees purity after four qadam have passed from the sun’s zenith, then she should not pray except al-ʿAṣr, because the time of al-Ẓuhr came upon her while she was in blood, and its time left her while she was in blood; so it was not obligatory upon her to pray al-Ẓuhr. And what Allah has removed from her of the salat (prayer) while she is in blood is greater.”

He said: “And if the woman sees blood after four qadam have passed from the sun’s zenith, then she should refrain from the salat (prayer). Then when she becomes pure from the blood, she must make up al-Ẓuhr, because the time of al-Ẓuhr came upon her while she was pure, and the time of al-Ẓuhr left her while she was pure, so she neglected the salat (prayer) of al-Ẓuhr, and thus making it up became obligatory upon her.”

key_terms.أَرْبَعَةُ أَقْدَامٍ: a measured portion of time after zenith mentioned as the legal threshold in this ruling
key_terms.الدَّمِ: menstrual blood, which prevents the obligation of salat (prayer)
key_terms.الطُّهْرَ: ritual purity after the cessation of menstrual blood
key_terms.زَوَالِ الشَّمْسِ: the sun’s decline from the meridian, the beginning of al-Ẓuhr time
key_terms.غُرُوبِ الشَّمْسِ: sunset, marking the approach of the end of daytime prayer periods

ai.seo_question: If a woman becomes pure or starts menstruation late in the day, which prayers must she perform or make up?
ai.summary: This hadith gives a legal ruling about a menstruating woman who either becomes pure or begins bleeding during the time of al-Ẓuhr. It explains when al-Ẓuhr is waived and when it must be made up, based on whether she was in a state of blood or purity during its effective prayer time.
